newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela comptroller says corruption increasing.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela comptroller says corruption increasing.

text.p: Corruption in Venezuela's public administration continues to spread despite official pledges to stamp it out, Venezuela's top official watchdog said Wednesday.

"Sadly we have to acknowledge that corruption has not decreased...it has continued and increased," Comptroller General Eduardo Roche Lander told reporters after presenting his annual report to Congress.
President Rafael Caldera was elected in 1993 on a platform of honest government and a pledge to clamp down on Venezuela's notorious levels of corruption.

But despite raising the fight against corruption at international forums and nominating a special commissioner to investigate cases in the public sector, Caldera's efforts have been largely ineffective, Roche Lander said.
"The actions of the government to reduce corruption are inefficient," he said.

The Comptroller's office carried out 3,000 investigations in 1996 into cases which included the use of state oil company planes by public officials, government aid given to banks with liquidity problems, and irregularities carried out under the system of exchange controls.
Roche Lander said his definition of corruption also extended to inefficiency and inadequate public services.
The Comptroller General's report frequently criticizes the government, but rarely leads to public officials being formally charged with corruption.
